body:
### Problem

When a server returns a completion list in which most items have no `textEdit`, but **at least one** item has a `textEdit` whose range starts to the left of the client's word boundary, `adjust_start_col()` lowers the start column for the **entire list**. Items that carry a `textEdit` get the skipped text prepended in `_lsp_to_complete_items()`; items **without** a `textEdit` do not. Accepting one of those overwrites the skipped text.

In practice, with TypeScript 7 native (`tsc --lsp`), completing a member on a `string` deletes the `.`:

```
foo.<C-x><C-o><C-y>   ->  footoString      (expected: foo.toString)
```

### Steps to reproduce

```sh
mkdir nvim-completion-repro && cd nvim-completion-repro
npm init -y && npm i typescript@7
printf '{"compilerOptions":{"strict":true,"target":"esnext","module":"esnext"},"include":["src"]}' > tsconfig.json
mkdir src && printf 'const foo = "bar";\nfoo.\n' > src/a.ts
```

`minimal_init.lua`:

```lua
vim.lsp.config('tsc', {
  cmd = { vim.fn.getcwd() .. '/node_modules/.bin/tsc', '--lsp', '--stdio' },
  filetypes = { 'typescript' },
  root_markers = { 'tsconfig.json' },
})
vim.lsp.enable('tsc')
```

```sh
nvim --clean -u minimal_init.lua src/a.ts
```

Put the cursor at end of line 2 (just after `foo.`), enter insert mode, then `<C-x><C-o>` and `<C-y>`.

**Expected:** `foo.toString`
**Actual:** `footoString` — the `.` is deleted the moment the menu opens.

`vim.lsp.completion.enable()` is affected identically (with `noselect` it only looks fine until you actually select an item).

### Why this particular list triggers it

For `foo.` with the cursor at 0-indexed character 4, tsgo returns 52 items:

- **51** have no `textEdit`, no `insertText`, no `filterText` — only a `label` (`toString`, `concat`, `length`, …).
- **1** item, `Symbol` (for `[Symbol.iterator]`), has `textEdit.range = (1,3)-(1,4)` and `newText` starting `[Symbol`. That range covers the `.`, which is correct for that item — bracket notation has to replace the dot.

### Root cause

- `adjust_start_col()` returns the **minimum** `textEdit` start across all items → `3`, so `server_start_boundary = 3` for every item.
- `trigger()` then calls `vim.fn.complete()` with `start_col = server_start_boundary + 1 = 4`, i.e. at the `.`.
- The compensation in `_lsp_to_complete_items()` that prepends the skipped text is guarded on `item.textEdit`, so the 51 label-only items keep a bare `word`.
- `_lsp_to_complete_items()` also does not receive the client word boundary at all — it is not in its parameter list, so there is no value to fall back to.

Instrumented on v0.12.5 (`runtime/lua/vim/lsp/completion.lua`):

```
CONVERT label=toString  server_start_boundary=3  client_start_boundary=nil  lnum=1  line="foo."  hasTextEdit=false  word="toString"
CONVERT label=Symbol    server_start_boundary=3  client_start_boundary=nil  lnum=1  line="foo."  hasTextEdit=true   word="[Symbol]"
TRIGGER  server_start_boundary=3  word_boundary=4  start_col=4
```

`word_boundary` (4) is correct; it is discarded in favour of the shifted server boundary.

### Notes

- This is **not** tsgo-specific — any server that returns a mixed list is affected. Completing `process.` does *not* reproduce, because `process` has no `Symbol` member and 0/85 of its items carry a `textEdit`; the bug requires the mixed list.
- Sending label-only items alongside per-item ranges is valid LSP, and clients are expected to apply each item's range individually.
- The "items without explicit `textEdit` being corrupted" failure mode is already mentioned in passing in the #32142 discussion (lemminx, clangd), but there does not appear to be a standalone issue or minimal repro for it.

### Possible fix

Thread the client word boundary into `_lsp_to_complete_items()` and use it as `item_start_byte` when an item has no `textEdit`, so the existing missing-prefix logic covers those items too. I tested this locally against v0.12.5 (3 hunks: add the parameter, pass it at the call site in `_convert_results()`, drop the `item.textEdit` guard with a fallback). It fixes the case above (`foo.toString`, and `foo.endsWith` after `<C-n>`) with no change to the `process.` case (0 `textEdit`s) — happy to open a PR if that approach looks right.

### Related

- #32142 (draft, milestone 0.13) — `editsNearCursor`; discussion notes this same corruption
- #30905 — wrong startcol when the label is not a keyword
- #24646 — historical "extra `.` when completing with tsserver"

### Version

```
NVIM v0.12.5
Build type: Release
LuaJIT 2.1.1774638290
```
macOS 15 (Darwin 25.6.0) arm64 · `typescript@7.0.2` (`tsc --lsp --stdio`)

comment_data.body: thanks for referencing other issues, that's helpful. but just to confirm, please test latest nightly (0.13) because there has been a lot of work in this area.

Tested on nightly — **fixed there.** Thanks for the pointer.

Same repro as in the issue, identical keys (`--clean -u minimal_init.lua`, cursor after `foo.`, `<C-x><C-o>` then `<C-y>`):

| Version | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `v0.12.5` (release) | `footoString` |
| `v0.13.0-dev-1511+g5209695703` | `foo.toString` |

For anyone finding this later, the relevant change is in `_lsp_to_complete_items()`: it now takes a `default_start_byte` parameter ("0-indexed start byte for items without an edit range"), the `and item.textEdit` condition is gone from the compensation guard, and the prefix is sliced per item:

```lua
local start_char = edit_start_char(item, lnum)
local start_byte = start_char and vim.str_byteindex(line, encoding, start_char, false)
  or default_start_byte
if start_byte and start_byte > server_start_boundary then
  pad = line:sub(server_start_boundary + 1, start_byte)
  item_prefix = prefix:sub(#pad + 1)
end
```

That covers the label-only items my report was about, and the per-item `item_prefix` goes further than the fix I'd sketched. Happy for this to be closed as already fixed — closing it myself to keep the tracker tidy, please reopen if you'd rather track the backport.

One separate thing I noticed while testing, which reproduces on the same nightly and is *not* fixed: with `vim.lsp.completion.enable(..., { autotrigger = true })`, pressing `<BS>` dismisses the menu permanently instead of re-finding matches. `:h popupmenu-keys` documents `<BS>` as "find the matches for the shorter word before the cursor. This may find more matches." Isolated on `v0.13.0-dev-1511`, same config, only difference is one `<BS>`:

- `myHelpe` → `<C-x><C-o>` → `<C-n><C-y>` → `myHelperFunction`
- `myHelpe` → `<C-x><C-o>` → `<BS>` → `<C-n><C-y>` → `myHelp` (menu gone; 3/3 runs)

The autotrigger path only hooks `InsertCharPre`, which never fires for deletions, and `vim.lsp.omnifunc` returns `-2` and calls `complete()` asynchronously, so it has no Dict on which to set `{"refresh": "always"}` (`:h 'complete'`). Want me to open that as its own issue, or is it already covered by the ongoing work in this area?

title: LSP completion: items without `textEdit` are corrupted when another item's `textEdit` moves the shared start boundary (trigger char deleted)
